description: Sources confirming Brazilian iGeo contestants + results, per edition (partial coverage).

provenanceClasses.official: geoolympiad.org results PDFs (gold medallists + team rankings).
provenanceClasses.primary: OBG Instagram/Facebook posts; school and press news; NOIC.

globalNotes: Editions attended: 2016, 2018, 2019, 2022-2026 (8; 2017 skipped, 2020 cancelled, 2021 online edition not entered). Brazilian medals: bronze 2024, 2025, 2026.

COVERAGE IS PARTIAL: iGeo's official results list only gold medallists, so Brazilian rosters depend on OBG (Olimpíada Brasileira de Geografia) posts, schools and press. 2019 and 2023 have no usable names; 2018 has 3 of 4 and 2026 3 of 4; 2016 (3 of 3), 2022, 2024 and 2025 are complete. OBG's old site (unifal-mg.edu.br/obgeografia) returns HTTP 410 and its Instagram is only partly indexed (anonymous visitors see the three newest posts).

TEAM SIZE: up to four students per country is the iGeo rule (OBG's own page: 'equipes de quatro alunos e dois mentores'), but that is a cap, not evidence for a given year - the 2016 debut team was three. Edition-specific statements were found for 2016 (UNIFAL-MG and CREDE-01/SEDUC-CE, three students), 2018 (Comando Militar do Planalto), 2023 (Unicamp IG), 2024 (FACEPE names all four) and 2026 (Colégio Militar de Fortaleza, post-event, and Colégio Motiva); 2022 and 2025 rest on the OBG rosters already recorded. 2019 remains unverified.

Selection via the OBG national final (UNIFAL-MG, later Unicamp): a written round, a paper and simulated tests in English; travel depends on funding, so a year's team can be smaller than the rule allows.

ATTENDANCE (2026-09-18 pass): because most Brazilian names come from selection announcements, every named student was re-checked against evidence published during or after the competition. Confirmed: all four for 2025 and, for 2026, Bianca Ribas and Theodora Flor (Tiago Sales was already confirmed by his medal). Still pre-event only: all three named 2018 students (Marina Hutzler, Lucas Caetano Filippo and Guilherme Lomba Shittine) - no source places any of them in Quebec City. 2016, 2022, 2023 and 2024 rest on items written after their editions.

years.note: Beijing (debut, 16-22 Aug), roster resolved 2026-09-17. The three students all came from one school, EEEP Salaberga Torquato Gomes de Matos (Maranguape-CE), and were selected through the 2nd OBG 2016 (35,917 students / 1,184 schools); the team leaders were Clibson Alves dos Santos (UNIFAL-MG) and Roberto Greco (Unicamp), and CNPq paid for the trip. TEAM SIZE 3, not 4, stated twice: UNIFAL-MG's press office ('por três alunos do ensino médio', against a cap the same item gives as 'uma equipe de até 4 alunos e 2 professores') and CREDE 01 / SEDUC-CE ('Os participantes são os únicos estudantes brasileiros na Olimpíada'). No medals ('apesar dos alunos não terem conquistado medalhas'). TRAP 1: surnames exist in exactly one source - UNIFAL-MG - and its live URL (unifal-mg.edu.br/comunicacao/universidadeparticipadeolimpiadainternacionaldegeografia) now returns HTTP 500 from a Drupal/MySQL disk error, so the Wayback capture is cited; the live UNIFAL-MG Geography news archive is kept as the pointer to it. TRAP 2: the third student's surname is UNRESOLVED - UNIFAL-MG writes 'Gabriella Abreu' while CREDE-01 and the school both write 'Gabriella Vital'; the record uses the UNIFAL-MG form because that item is the one that gives surnames for the whole team, and the two forms were NOT merged. TRAP 3: CREDE-01's archived page is entity-encoded (ú etc.), so only accent-free needles verify against it. TRAP 4: the old OBG site obgeografia.org is alive (HTTP 200, not 410 - that is the later unifal-mg.edu.br/obgeografia address) but its 2015/2016/2017 edition pages carry no international roster.

sources.confirms: iGeo official results: gold medallists and team rankings only (no Brazilian entry)

Colégio Núcleo (Recife) Facebook, 2018-07-19, PRE-EVENT: 'Marina Hutzler conquistou o 1º lugar do Brasil na iGEO (Olimpíada Internacional de Geografia) e vai representar o país na próxima etapa, dessa vez no Canadá. Ela embarca no próximo dia 29' - read in the browser 2026-09-18 (the post is a login shell to plain fetches)

Comando Militar do Planalto (2018-06-05, host now refuses connections; text via search index): Lucas Caetano Filippo and Guilherme Lomba Shittine (Colégio Militar de Brasília, 3rd year) selected for the four-student team representing Brazil at the iGeo in Quebec - the only team-size statement found for 2018

Jornal O Garanca no. 2 (Colegio Militar de Brasilia internal newsletter, Aug 2018), p. 3 'Alunos do CMB sao destaque em Olimpiada Brasileira de Geografia': Lucas Caetano Filippo and Guilherme Lomba, both 3o A/EM, 'foram selecionados para compor a equipe de quatro estudantes que representara o Brasil na Olimpiada Internacional de Geografia, a ser realizada em Quebec - Canada'; OBG 2017 gold medallists who sat the English-language international selection in 2018 - read in the Calameo viewer 2026-09-17 (pre-event wording; the text is not exposed to plain fetches)

years.note: Quebec City. Marina Hutzler (Colégio Núcleo) plus Lucas Caetano Filippo and Guilherme Lomba Shittine (Colégio Militar de Brasília), from the Comando Militar do Planalto item of 2018-06-05; that item also states the team had four students, which is the team-size evidence for 2018. TRAP: every Brazilian-Army copy of that item is unreachable - cmp.eb.mil.br resets the connection, depa.eb.mil.br/noticias/227-... returns 403 and eb.mil.br/.../content/id/8928063 is a 404 with no Wayback capture; the text is only readable through the search index. VERIFIED 2026-09-17 in the Calameo viewer: the CMB newsletter O Garanca no. 2 (Aug 2018, p. 3) prints the same story - both names and 'equipe de quatro estudantes' - so the two CMB names no longer rest on a snippet alone, though both CMB sources are pre-event selection announcements (no post-event source confirms they travelled). Fourth member unknown. ATTENDANCE STILL UNCONFIRMED for all three after the 2026-09-18 pass - every 2018 source is a selection/send-off announcement, including Colégio Núcleo's, which is dated 2018-07-19 and says Marina Hutzler 'vai representar o país ... Ela embarca no próximo dia 29': the rest of the CMB's own Calaméo archive was read page by page (O Garança 3rd and 4th editions and the 124-page Revista CMB 2018, all posted Feb 2019, plus the July 2019 issue) and none of them mentions Quebec, the iGeo or any olympiad of geography - issue 2's pre-event note is the only CMB print mention of the trip; the Wayback Machine was offline that day, so the unreachable Army copies could not be retried from an archive. Incidental: the Revista CMB 2018 roll of pupils spells the second student 'Guilherme Schittine Bezerra Lomba' (Sch-, against the record's 'Shittine').

sources.confirms: iGeo 2023 official results: 45 teams / 177 students; gold medallists and team rankings only, but Brazil appears under 'Favourite poster selected by students' - positive proof a Brazilian team competed

Unicamp IG (co-organizer of the national final): the English test would be one of the marks used 'para a seleção de quatro estudantes que vão formar a equipe brasileira na 19ª Olimpíada Internacional de Geografia' in Bandung 2023 - team size, no names

years.note: Bandung. Still no names. Two things were settled: Brazil definitely competed (the official results name Brazil among the 'favourite poster' winners) and the team was four students (Unicamp IG, co-organizer of the national final, on the selection that followed the December 2022 final).

years.note: Dublin/Maynooth. First Brazilian iGeo medal (bronze, Pablo Fernando de Azurza Nogueira e Gómez Alvarez - A Tribuna's 'Pablo Fernando de Azurza Nogueira Gomez' and NOIC's 'Pablo Alvarez' are short forms). Roster completed 2026-09-16 from FACEPE/UNIFAL-MG, which names the full team of four and so also settles the team size: the two members A Tribuna left unnamed are Davi de Magalhães Vianna Navarro (Colégio Militar de Belo Horizonte) and Valentina Vale Farias Cruz (Colégio Militar de Fortaleza); Gabriel Volpato Lima and Pablo are from Colégio FAESA (Vitória).

years.note: Bangkok. Roster first recorded from the OBG selection announcement; ATTENDANCE CONFIRMED for all four on 2026-09-18, each from a source published after the competition ended: Isabela Granado from her school's own post (Colégio Santa Rosa, 01/08), Bárbara Pinheiro Puget Cruz and Clara Gonzalez Ferreira Pinto Sampaio from Movimento Meninas Olímpicas (01/08, 'compuseram a equipe'), and João Lucas Dantas Barbosa from his NOIC staff biography ('a disputar a iGeo 2025 em Bangkok') plus the NOIC iGeo guide he co-wrote, which is illustrated with Bangkok 2025 closing-ceremony, exam and poster photographs. Isabela Granado Santos's bronze (second Brazilian medal) no longer rests on the 2026-08 DATA_STATUS verification alone - the school post states it outright. TRAP: the Meninas Olímpicas post mis-types the dates as '26 de junho e 1 de agosto'; every other source puts the edition in late July-1 August 2025. The @igeo.brazil Instagram account that the 2025 team set up (cited in the NOIC guide) has since been removed.

sources.confirms: Colégio Militar de Fortaleza Instagram, 2026-08-18, POST-EVENT: Tiago Sales bronze at iGeo 2026 (Istanbul, 10-17 Aug), Brazil's only 2026 medal and third ever; the same post states 'a equipe brasileira representada por quatro alunos', the only post-event team-size statement for 2026 (caption pasted by the maintainer 2026-09-19: 'a equipe brasileira representada por quatro alunos, entre os quais o Aluno Tiago Sales ... que conquistou a medalha de bronze na competicao individual')

OBG Instagram, 2026-08-15: 'A equipe brasileira já está na Turquia e participou da cerimônia de abertura da Olimpíada Internacional de Geografia nesta segunda-feira dia 10/08' - event-day proof that a Brazilian team was in Istanbul, but the caption names nobody (re-read in the browser 2026-09-18)

Sul in Foco (SC), 2026-08-11 (EVENT DAY): 'A estudante lagunense Theodora Flor já está em Istambul, na Turquia, onde representa o Brasil na Olimpíada Internacional de Geografia (iGeo) 2026. A competição segue até a próxima segunda-feira (17)'; the same item adds 'A equipe do país também conta com representantes de Brasília, Fortaleza e Paraíba', which places the still-unnamed fourth member in Brasília
sources.needle: Theodora Flor já está em Istambul

years.note: Istanbul (10-17 Aug 2026). Tiago Sales (Colégio Militar de Fortaleza) bronze - Brazil's third medal. ATTENDANCE CONFIRMED 2026-09-18 for the other two named members from items published while the olympiad was running: Bianca Ribas 'está representando o Brasil ... em Istambul' (her school, 13/08) and Theodora Flor 'já está em Istambul' (Sul in Foco, 11/08). Team size 4 is now stated post-event by the Colégio Militar de Fortaleza. The fourth member is STILL UNNAMED, but Sul in Foco places the delegation's home cities as Laguna, Brasília, Fortaleza and Paraíba - so the missing student is from Brasília, and no press or school item naming a Brasília student surfaced. OBG's Instagram documents the trip without ever naming anyone: 08/08 'O Brasil já está a caminho da Turquia', 15/08 opening ceremony, 21/08 wrap-up 'Chegamos ao fim da iGeo 2026'. TRAPS: geoolympiad.org has published no 2026 results document (its results library still stops at 2025); FACEPE still has no 2026 article; and Agora Laguna ran the same 11/08 'está em Istambul' story but sits behind a Cloudflare challenge that 403s plain fetches, so Sul in Foco is cited instead.
